diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $M>0$, and $r$ be some integer such that $2^{s-1}<r\leq 2^s$ for some integer $s\geq 1$.
There exists a sequence of transformer blocks $B_i\in\mathcal{B}(2^{\lfloor (i-1)/3 \rfloor}D,3,d_{embed})$, $i=1,\cdots,3s$, such that
For power series, it suffices to show for the case $r=2^s$ as well.

issues.failure_explanation: The induction only constructs the dyadic powers (x^1)^{2^k}. For a non-dyadic integer r with 2^{s-1}<r<2^s, the 2^s-power does not determine the r-power, and computing the higher dyadic power can even require intermediate magnitudes larger than the lemma's hypothesis max_{i,j<=r}{||x||^i+||x||^j}<M when ||x||_infty>1. No binary-expansion, truncation, or addition-chain argument is supplied for the stated general r.

failure_location.quote: It suffices to show for the case $r=2^s$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict Lemma lemrpower, and the general-r part of Lemma lemdiv, to dyadic r and round the division truncation length up to the next power of two, or add a binary-exponentiation argument proving arbitrary r<=2^s within the same O(log r) block/head bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone exact componentwise r-th power claim, and the general-r power-series part of Lemma lemdiv that relies on it, are unproved as stated. The main approximation argument can still go through if the truncation length is rounded up to a dyadic value, but that repair is not the stated lemma.
issues.title: Lemma lemrpower proves only dyadic exponents, not the stated general integer r
issues.why_classification: A contained repair exists and the main theorems survive by using dyadic truncation lengths, but the stated general-integer power lemma needs either a real new exponentiation argument or a limited weakening of its claim.

issues.failure_explanation: From ||T-f||_infty<=epsilon and ||f||_infty<=R, the triangle inequality gives only ||T||_infty<=R+epsilon, not the class requirement ||T||_infty<=R. No clipping construction or enlarged output bound is supplied, so the asserted membership T in mathcal T(...,R,kappa) is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use output bound R+epsilon in the transformer class, or explicitly construct clipping to [-R,R] that preserves the epsilon error, and carry the adjusted bound through the generalization proof; the advertised rates are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation theorem's formal class membership is unreliable, and the generalization theorem's ERM/covering arguments that use the same output bound R inherit the same mismatch until the bound is enlarged or clipping is constructed.
issues.title: thmApprox claims membership in an R-bounded transformer class while the construction only bounds the output by R+epsilon
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local parameter enlargement or clipping argument; the approximation rate, depth/width scaling, and final generalization rate survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By balancing the bias and variance, i.e., setting $\epsilon^2=\frac{\epsilon^{-\frac{d}{\alpha}}}{n}$, we get $\epsilon=n^{-\frac{\alpha}{2\alpha+d}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof sets epsilon=n^{-alpha/(2alpha+d)} and invokes thmApprox, but thmApprox is only stated for epsilon<min{1,(tau_M/2)^alpha}. For small n this epsilon can violate that range, and at n=1 the iterated logarithm ln(ln(n^{alpha/(2alpha+d)})) is ln(0). The theorem states the bound for n training samples with no sufficiently-large-n condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit hypothesis that n is large enough that n^{-alpha/(2alpha+d)} lies in thmApprox's epsilon interval, equivalently n>max{1,(2/tau_M)^{2alpha+d}}, and that the iterated logarithm is evaluated on a quantity greater than 1.
issues.overall_effect: As a statement valid for every n, thmGeneralization is not meaningful or not applicable for small n; the asymptotic rate itself is unaffected once the missing large-n regime is imposed.
issues.title: thmGeneralization substitutes epsilon=n^{-alpha/(2alpha+d)} without the large-n hypothesis required by thmApprox
issues.why_classification: This is a standard parameter-regime repair; adding the large-n condition preserves the stated rate and all dependent conclusions.
